Wait one minute to see if recovery occurs

A sign that CPR should be delayed

Sensitivity confirms acute periodontal abscess formation

4.q: A radiograph of the lower right posterior region shows an unexposed white area along the left side of the image. What is the most likely cause of this appearance?

Overexposure caused by excessive exposure time

n.3: Movement blur causes loss of sharpness, not a sharply outlined unexposed area.
n.4: Elongation alters tooth length and shape rather than producing a white side border.

4.q: Which action best supports staff safety during waste handling?
o: Using suitable PPE and hand hygiene
Opening bags to check contents manually

4.q: Which numbered item shows the materials most likely to include irrigants and endodontic consumables used chairside during treatment?

n.3: Item 4 is rubber dam isolation equipment.

5.q: Which record should be completed immediately after a successful cycle?

n.0: Holiday requests are unrelated.

n.3: Uniform checks do not document cycles.

5.q: A patient sips sugary fizzy drinks throughout the afternoon. What is the best dietary advice?

n.3: Brushing after every sip is impractical and does not address intake pattern.
n.4: Holding drinks in the mouth increases exposure time.

5.q: Which item is most appropriate basic equipment to assist ventilation during a medical emergency?

n.3: An endodontic ruler is unrelated to airway support.
n.4: A wax knife has no emergency airway function.

5.q: Which practice best protects the clean zone?
5.w: A dedicated clean storage area helps keep sterilised items separate from contamination sources.

n.0: Shared cloths may spread contamination.
n.2: Used trays should stay in dirty zones.
n.3: Waste should be separated from clean stock.

5.q: Which waste item is most suitable for general domestic waste if uncontaminated?

n.3: Biological waste requires specific handling.
n.4: Amalgam waste requires controlled disposal.

5.q: During treatment, a patient suddenly becomes pale, sweaty and says they feel faint after seeing the local anaesthetic needle. What is the most likely emergency being recognised?

n.2: Seizure would more commonly involve altered consciousness or convulsive activity.
n.3: Hyperglycaemia develops more gradually and commonly causes thirst or lethargy.
n.4: Anaphylaxis often includes airway, breathing or skin changes after exposure.

5.q: Which item should remain in the dirty zone until processed?
5.w: Used hand instruments are contaminated and belong in the dirty zone until decontaminated.

n.0: Labels are not contaminated instruments.
n.2: Wrapped cassettes may be clean processed stock.
n.3: Sterile packs belong in the clean zone.
n.4: Administrative sheets are not dirty-zone items.

5.q: A patient attends with a tongue ulcer that has been present for over 3 weeks and has not improved. What is the most appropriate action by the dental team?
o: Advise salt mouthrinses and review in 6 months
Record the finding and arrange urgent referral for further assessment
Polish the adjacent teeth and discharge the patient
Prescribe antibiotics as the main treatment
Reassure the patient that all tongue ulcers are harmless
5.w: A persistent ulcer present for more than 3 weeks requires urgent referral for assessment because oral cancer must be excluded.

n.0: A 6-month delay is inappropriate for a suspicious lesion.
n.2: Removing local factors may help in some cases, but a persistent lesion still requires urgent assessment.
n.3: Antibiotics are not the primary management for a suspicious persistent oral ulcer.
n.4: Persistent tongue ulcers are not all harmless and should not be dismissed.

5.q: Which combination of risk factors most significantly increases the likelihood of oral cancer?
o: Low sugar intake and fluoride use
5.w: Smoking and alcohol together significantly increase the risk of oral cancer due to their synergistic effects.

n.0: These are not risk factors for oral cancer.
n.2: These are protective behaviours.
n.3: These do not increase cancer risk.
n.4: These are beneficial for oral health.

5.q: Which item most likely requires specialist disposal rather than standard clinical waste?
5.w: Amalgam waste requires specialist disposal due to mercury content and environmental controls.

n.0: Paper bibs may enter another stream depending on contamination.
n.2: Wrappers are not specialist hazardous waste.
n.3: Clean cardboard is not specialist waste.
n.4: Cup lids are not specialist waste.

5.q: During placement of a composite restoration, the patient closes unexpectedly while instruments are in the mouth. What is the best action?
o: Continue quickly before the patient moves again
Withdraw instruments safely and check the patient
Ask the patient not to do that and proceed

n.3: The patient should be checked before continuing.

5.q: A patient swaps from fizzy cola to sweetened fruit juice and drinks it often. How should this be interpreted?

n.2: Risk depends on content and frequency.
n.3: Many sugary drinks can contribute to decay risk.
n.4: Sweet drinks are not equivalent to water.

5.q: A needle must be recapped because treatment is interrupted and it will be reused immediately. What is the best method?
o: Use a safer one-handed or device-assisted method
Ask patient to hold the cap

5.q: A patient is seated for an extraction and says they are unsure whether they want to continue. What is the best immediate action?

Ask the nurse to persuade the patient
Begin local anaesthetic quickly before they change their mind
Tell the patient they must continue

n.3: Starting treatment without clear consent is inappropriate.
n.4: Patients cannot be forced to continue elective treatment.

5.q: Using the image, identify instrument set number 2.

5.q: Which surface of the tooth shown in the image would be most prone to plaque accumulation due to pits and fissures?

Prepare for upper left first premolar treatment
Prepare for lower right first premolar treatment

n.3: Headrest covers are shaped differently.
n.4: Disposable napkins are not intended as sterile drapes.

5.q: Based on the image provided, which structure is the outermost protective layer of the crown?

5.q: A patient has central chest pain not relieved by their own GTN spray and looks clammy. What is the best management?

Continue treatment but shorten the appointment
Ask the patient to drive home and rest
Place them in the recovery position immediately

5.q: A yellow bag in the surgery contains blood-contaminated gauze and used PPE. What is the best action?

Empty it into a black sack
Store it under the sink indefinitely

o: Express a small amount first to ensure even flow from both pastes

Remove the mixing tip once the material starts flowing
Cool the cartridge on the glass slab for several minutes

5.q: A patient asks why their gums bleed even though they do not feel pain. Which is the best response?

Bleeding is a sign of gingival inflammation, even when there is no pain

Bleeding is caused by enamel erosion

5.q: A patient with visible plaque accumulation asks what contributes most to their gum disease. Which is the best response?

Carry it by hand to the decontamination room
Break the needle from the syringe first

Leave it for the next shift

9.q: Which item is being identified as unsuitable for mixing with sterile stock after processing?

9.q: Before exposing a dental radiograph, what is the primary reason for checking the patient's previous radiographs and records?

To select the darkest image available

Counting the number of lower molars present
Confirming that the teeth are mandibular molars

n.4: Tooth type can still be identified from overall morphology.

9.q: After condensation of amalgam, the dentist requests an instrument to reproduce grooves and occlusal anatomy. Which type is needed?

n.1: A condenser compacts material but does not create detailed anatomy effectively.

n.4: A probe is an examination instrument rather than a carving instrument.

9.q: A bin used for mixed recycling contains contaminated gloves. What error has occurred?

9.w: Contaminated PPE should not be placed in recycling waste.

n.0: This does not describe the error shown.
n.2: Bin size is not the main issue.
n.3: Lid colour may matter, but contamination is the key problem.
n.4: Room stock levels are unrelated.

9.q: A patient asks why fluoride toothpaste is recommended. What is the best explanation?
9.w: Fluoride helps strengthen enamel and reduce decay risk.

n.1: Whitening is not the main preventive reason.

9.q: Examine the radiograph. Which radiographic type is shown?

n.0: Horizontal bitewings show only posterior crowns and limited bone, not the entire jaws.
n.1: Vertical bitewings show increased bone height but not full jaw anatomy.
n.2: Periapical radiographs focus on a small number of teeth including apices, not the full dentition.

9.q: A sharps bin lid is cracked but still closes. What is the best action?
o: Replace it according to local policy

n.0: Visible damage should not be ignored.
n.1: Tape is not an approved fix.
n.3: Manual transfer of contents is unsafe.
n.4: Storage does not resolve the hazard.

9.q: Using the image, identify area number 6.

n.1: A pontic is an artificial replacement tooth.

n.3: Healthy papilla would not resemble a socket.

9.q: A dental nurse is assisting during a restoration of a molar where the chewing surface is being treated. Which surface is the dentist working on?

n.2: Overlapping contacts affect proximal contact clarity, not image margins.

9.q: Which item is most appropriate for grasping and removing a tooth crown during routine extraction?
9.w: Extraction forceps are designed to grip and remove teeth.

n.1: Needle holders are for suturing.
n.2: College tweezers handle small items.
n.3: Wax knives are laboratory instruments.
n.4: Spatulas are not extraction instruments.

9.q: During root canal treatment, the rubber dam tears near the clamp and saliva begins to leak into the field. What is the best action?
o: Continue quickly to complete the shaping before contamination increases
Inform the operator immediately so isolation can be re-established
Use high-volume suction only and continue treatment
Dry the area repeatedly with cotton pellets and proceed
Delay mentioning it until the canal has been dressed
9.w: Contamination during endodontic treatment is significant, so the operator should be informed immediately and proper isolation restored.

9.q: Which non-verbal behaviour is most likely to reassure an anxious patient?

n.3: Closed posture may seem unapproachable.
n.4: Leaving mid-conversation appears dismissive.

9.q: The apex locator display repeatedly gives unstable readings while the file is in the canal. What is the most likely interpretation?
o: The canal conditions or file position may be affecting the reading
The tooth must have fractured vertically
Obturation has already reached the correct apical level
The local anaesthetic is preventing accurate measurement
The working length can be assumed from the previous tooth
9.w: Unstable apex locator readings commonly suggest that canal conditions, contact or file position may be interfering with accurate measurement.

n.1: A vertical fracture cannot be concluded solely from unstable apex locator readings.
n.2: Unstable readings do not indicate that obturation has been correctly completed.
n.3: Local anaesthetic does not explain inconsistent electronic measurements in this way.

9.q: Which behaviour most increases workplace safety incidents in a busy practice?

n.4: Prompt reporting helps control risks.

9.q: Using the image, what is item number 4 most likely associated with?

n.1: Obturation kits contain endodontic materials.

n.3: Debond packs contain orthodontic tools.
n.4: Oxygen units are unrelated emergency equipment.

9.q: A parent says their 7-year-old child brushes alone and often misses evening brushing. Which advice is most appropriate?

The child should brush only in the morning until technique improves
Use mouthwash instead of evening brushing
Allow the child to brush longer without supervision
Change to a harder toothbrush so more plaque is removed
9.w: Children often need supervision and assistance to achieve effective plaque removal, especially for bedtime brushing.

n.4: A traumatic tattoo is a pigmentation finding and does not explain the periodontal contour changes.

o: Seat the crown quickly before the cement starts to set
Improve isolation and alert the operator that contamination has occurred
Dry only the fitting surface of the crown and continue as planned
Add more cement to compensate for moisture contamination

Ask no questions and assume agreement

Discard the mix and prepare a fresh one using the correct ratio
Add extra liquid slowly until the mix looks smoother
Use the incorrect mix only as a lining material instead
Mix for a shorter time so the material is not overworked

10.q: Which description best identifies a red flag feature for oral cancer?

A small traumatic ulcer that resolves after adjustment of a denture
A transient white coating that can be wiped away
A symmetrical pigmentation present since childhood

10.q: A patient is hyperventilating, anxious and tingling in the fingers but remains responsive. What is the best immediate action?

10.q: Which instrument type is most appropriate for carrying freshly mixed amalgam from the well to the prepared cavity?

Send the patient home alone at once
Give GTN spray to prevent relapse
Lay the patient flat for one hour regardless of condition
11.w: After recovery, continued monitoring and follow-up carbohydrate intake may help maintain glucose levels.

n.1: Immediate treatment restart may be inappropriate.
n.2: Abrupt discharge without reassessment may be unsafe.
n.3: GTN has no role in hypoglycaemia management.
n.4: Positioning should reflect the patient's condition, not a fixed rule.

11.q: Which behaviour most increases patient management problems in practice?
11.w: Rushing patients often leads to anxiety, confusion and dissatisfaction.

n.0: Clear explanations usually improve management.
n.2: Checking comfort supports positive care.
n.3: Listening helps address issues early.
n.4: Organisation reduces avoidable problems.

11.q: A patient with periodontal concerns asks where to focus cleaning first. What is the best action?
o: Explain cleaning at the gum margin and between teeth is especially important
Advise brushing only the biting surfaces
Advise replacing brushing with chewing gum
11.w: Plaque commonly accumulates at the gingival margin and interdentally, so these areas need attention.

n.1: Cleaning only biting surfaces misses common plaque-retentive areas.
n.2: Bleeding areas often need improved cleaning, not avoidance.
n.3: Toothpaste may be beneficial but this does not address cleaning focus.
n.4: Chewing gum is not a substitute for brushing.

11.q: Which sequence best reflects correct movement of instruments through workflow?
11.w: Contaminated instruments are received, cleaned, sterilised and then stored ready for use.

n.0: Storage should not occur before cleaning.
n.2: Cleaning precedes sterilisation.
n.3: Storage should follow decontamination.
n.4: Packaging and use are in the wrong order.

11.q: Which anatomical or pathological feature is most appropriately assessed on the image shown?
o: Floor of mouth structures and localisation of radiopaque objects
Apical pathology of upper incisors only
11.w: Lower occlusal views are useful for assessing the mandibular arch, floor of mouth region and localising radiopaque objects such as calculi.

n.1: Upper premolar proximal caries are better assessed with bitewing radiographs.
n.2: TMJs are not shown on this occlusal image.
n.3: This is not the preferred image for isolated upper incisor apical assessment.
n.4: Soft tissue profile is assessed with cephalometric imaging.

11.q: A dental nurse is assisting during periodontal charting. The patient has bleeding on probing, recession and calculus deposits around the lower incisors. Which condition is most consistent with these findings?
o: Periodontitis affecting the lower anterior region
11.w: Bleeding on probing with recession and calculus in this context is most consistent with periodontitis affecting the lower anterior teeth.

n.0: Gingivitis alone does not account for the recession and periodontal support loss implied by the presentation.
n.2: A periapical abscess is related to pulpal infection and usually presents differently.
n.3: Oral candidosis affects mucosal tissues rather than causing calculus-associated periodontal destruction.
n.4: Irreversible pulpitis causes pulpal pain and is not diagnosed from gingival recession and calculus.

11.q: Which item should remain furthest from the clean storage area?
11.w: Used instrument receiving trays belong in the contaminated intake area, away from clean storage.

n.0: Labels may be used in clean areas.
n.2: Sealed pouches belong in clean storage.
n.3: Clean cassette racks should remain in clean areas.
n.4: Records may be kept in a clean admin area.

11.q: Which observation most strongly suggests a clean zone is being maintained correctly?
11.w: A clean zone containing only sealed processed packs indicates good segregation control.

n.0: Used trays should not be near the clean zone.
n.2: Waste bags do not belong in clean storage areas.
n.3: Dirty gloves indicate contamination.
n.4: Open exposed instruments lose protected status.

11.q: The panoramic radiograph shows a broad radiolucent band over the apices of the maxillary teeth. What is the most likely cause of this error?
o: Patient failed to place the tongue against the palate
11.w: A palatoglossal air space appears as a dark band over the maxillary apices when the tongue is not held against the palate during exposure.

n.1: Movement causes blurring or double outlines rather than a defined radiolucent band.
n.2: Lead apron artefact is usually radiopaque and lower in the image.
n.3: Short exposure reduces density but does not create this characteristic air space.
n.4: A reversed receptor would not create a horizontal dark band over the maxillary roots.

11.q: A repeat panoramic radiograph is required after obtaining an image similar to this one. What is the best action before retaking it?
o: Instruct the patient to press the tongue firmly against the palate throughout exposure
Ask the patient to open wider during exposure
11.w: The correct preventive action is clear instruction for the patient to keep the tongue against the palate until the scan finishes.

n.0: Changing mA affects exposure, not palatoglossal air space.
n.2: The bite block assists positioning and is unrelated to this error.
n.3: Opening wider does not eliminate the air space.
n.4: Lowering the chin changes head position, not tongue posture.

11.q: A patient with periodontal pockets is anxious about treatment noise. What is the best supportive action by the nurse?
11.w: Clear reassurance and explanation can reduce anxiety and improve cooperation.

n.1: Leaving the patient unsupported is inappropriate.
n.2: Extra noise may worsen anxiety.
n.3: Questions should be answered appropriately.
n.4: Unexpected treatment may increase distress.

11.q: Which advice best helps prevent denture staining?
11.w: Regular appropriate cleaning helps reduce staining and plaque accumulation.

n.1: Boiling may distort acrylic.
n.2: Heat may damage the denture.
n.3: Abrasives can scratch surfaces.
n.4: Skipping brushing encourages deposits.

12.q: The image shows pus accumulation at the root apex. What is this composed of?
12.w: Pus consists of bacteria, dead tissue, and inflammatory cells.

n.0: Saliva is not involved in abscess formation.
n.2: Enamel proteins are not part of pus.
n.3: Pus is not composed of blood alone.
n.4: Fluoride does not form pus.

12.q: Which behaviour most undermines voluntary consent?
o: Pressuring the patient by saying they have no choice
12.w: Consent must be freely given without coercion or undue pressure.

n.0: Questions support informed decisions.
n.2: Written information can support understanding.
n.3: Checking understanding is good practice.
n.4: Options help support choice.

12.q: A dental nurse notices swelling and redness near a decayed tooth. What is the correct action?
o: Record findings and alert the dentist
12.w: The nurse must report findings to the dentist for diagnosis and management.

n.0: Diagnosis is outside scope.
n.2: Prescription is not within scope.
n.3: Swelling must not be ignored.
n.4: Whitening is irrelevant.

12.q: Which management error regarding emergency drugs and equipment is most serious?
o: Not knowing where the emergency kit is stored
Training staff to locate the AED
12.w: If staff cannot locate the emergency kit quickly, critical treatment may be dangerously delayed.

n.1: Routine expiry checks are good practice.
n.2: Replacing used stock is appropriate and necessary.
n.3: Checklists support readiness rather than create risk.
n.4: Training staff to find the AED improves emergency response.

12.q: A stock tray is overloaded and excess impression material repeatedly causes gagging. What is the best action?
o: Select the correct tray and load an appropriate amount of material
Use the same tray but increase the amount to improve retention
Seat the tray more slowly to let the patient adapt
Keep the tray in place longer before fully seating
Choose a darker shade of impression material
12.w: Correct tray selection and appropriate loading reduce overflow, improve comfort and still allow adequate recording.

n.1: Increasing the amount would likely worsen overflow and gagging.
n.2: Slower seating does not solve overloading.
n.3: Delaying seating is unlikely to improve the situation and may affect accuracy.
n.4: Shade is irrelevant to impression tray loading.

12.q: Which storage practice best supports COSHH compliance?
o: Products stored in original labelled containers
12.w: Original labelled containers help preserve identification, instructions and safe handling information.

n.0: Drink bottles create serious misidentification risk.
n.2: Removing lids increases spill risk.
n.3: Chemicals should be separated from food areas.
n.4: Open cups are unsafe storage.

12.q: When item 12 is used, why should the orange shield be positioned correctly?
o: To reduce exposure to the intense blue curing light
To improve retention of the impression tray
To prevent the composite from becoming too cold
To increase the etching effect on enamel
To stop alginate setting too quickly
12.w: The orange shield helps protect eyes from the intense blue light emitted during curing.

n.1: Tray retention depends on fit and impression material handling, not the curing light shield.
n.2: The shield does not control composite temperature.
n.3: Etching is performed chemically, not by the shield.
n.4: Alginate setting is unrelated to the curing light shield.

12.q: Which item is most important to bring first when responding to a collapsed patient elsewhere in the practice?
o: Emergency drugs kit and AED if available
12.w: Emergency response equipment such as the AED and emergency kit should be prioritised.

n.1: Administrative items are not immediate priorities.
n.2: Routine dental instruments are not first-line emergency equipment.
n.3: These may help later but are not priorities.
n.4: Impression materials are unrelated.

12.q: Which sequence best reflects safe handling of confidential paperwork?
o: Leave it on the desk overnight, then sort later
Collect it promptly, store securely, dispose of it appropriately when no longer needed
Photocopy it for interest, then file it
Take it home to complete later
Leave it in the waiting room tray
12.w: Confidential documents should be controlled, securely stored and disposed of through approved methods.

n.0: Unattended documents may be accessed by others.
n.2: Copying without need may breach confidentiality.
n.3: Taking records home may be inappropriate and insecure.
n.4: Waiting rooms are unsuitable for confidential records.

12.q: A periapical radiograph of the lower molar region shows the apices visible but a radiopaque band crossing the lower part of the image. What is the most likely explanation for this appearance?
o: The patient’s finger or receptor holder has been superimposed on the image
Periapical pathology affecting the mandibular molar roots
Cone cut due to poor beam alignment
12.w: A distinct radiopaque band crossing part of the image is most consistent with superimposition of a finger, holder component or other external object during exposure.

n.1: Periapical pathology appears around root apices, not as a straight radiopaque band across the image.
n.2: Mandibular cortex anatomy would not present as an isolated superimposed band.
n.3: Chemical fog reduces contrast more generally rather than creating a defined radiopaque strip.
n.4: Cone cut creates an unexposed pale or white area, not a dense superimposed band.

12.q: Based on the image, which stage of caries is shown?
12.w: The cavitation and depth indicate advanced dentine involvement.

n.0: The tooth is clearly not sound.
n.1: This stage is earlier and non-cavitated.
n.2: Moderate lesions are less extensive.
n.4: Arrested caries appears inactive.

12.q: Which interpretation best describes the recession seen in the image?
12.w: Recession indicates loss of periodontal attachment and supporting tissues.

n.0: Eruption does not cause recession in adults.
n.2: Enamel defects do not affect gingiva.
n.3: Orthodontics alone does not explain inflammation.
n.4: Pulpal pathology affects internal structures.

12.q: The presence of the microscope in the setup most likely supports which aspect of treatment?
o: Improved magnification and identification of canal anatomy
Chemical irrigation of the canal space
12.w: An operating microscope improves magnification and illumination, helping the operator identify canal anatomy and work more precisely.

n.1: File sterilisation is part of decontamination procedures and is not performed by the microscope.
n.2: Electronic working length measurement is carried out by an apex locator, not the microscope.
n.3: Irrigation depends on endodontic solutions and syringes, not on optical magnification.
n.4: The microscope does not alter obturation material consistency.

12.q: Which item is being identified as a post-cycle monitoring aid?
12.w: Chemical indicator strips help show exposure to specified sterilisation conditions.

n.0: Sharps bins are waste containers.
n.2: Hand towels are not cycle monitors.
n.3: A tap is unrelated to steriliser monitoring.
n.4: Protective glasses are PPE.

12.q: Which item should move last in a correctly organised workflow?
12.w: Placement of sterile packs into clean storage is the final stage after processing.

n.0: Used burs enter the process as contaminated items.
n.2: Tray liners are disposed of during dirty stages.
n.3: Dirty instruments start the workflow.
n.4: Waste removal is not the final clean output stage.

12.q: What is the best sequence once suturing is complete?
12.w: Instrument checks and safe tidying of the field should follow completion.

n.1: The surgery should be made safe before dismissal.
n.2: Alginate impressions are unrelated.
n.3: Records should be maintained, not removed.
n.4: Suction changes are not the priority stated.

12.q: Interpret the lesion shown in the image.
o: A normal variation of the dorsal tongue
A suspicious ulcerative lesion requiring urgent investigation
A benign mucocele of the lower lip
A physiological fissure of the tongue
A simple coating of the tongue surface
12.w: The lesion is ulcerative, irregular and clinically suspicious, so it requires urgent investigation.

n.0: Normal variation would not present as a destructive irregular ulcer.
n.2: A mucocele typically affects minor salivary gland sites such as the lip and has a different appearance.
n.3: A fissured tongue does not present as a red-white ulcerated lesion.
n.4: A tongue coating is superficial and does not produce this ulcerated appearance.

12.q: Which sign after extraction should be reported promptly to the clinician?
12.w: Persistent bleeding requires prompt review and management.

n.1: Temporary numbness may relate to anaesthetic early on.
n.2: Taste alone is not urgent.
n.3: Mild tiredness may be nonspecific.
n.4: Minor fullness can occur postoperatively.

12.q: Which sign would most help temporary staff maintain zones?
12.w: Clear clean and dirty area signs help staff identify where items should and should not be placed.

n.0: Break rotas do not guide zoning.
n.2: Wi-Fi details are unrelated.
n.3: Parking maps do not support decontamination control.
n.4: Uniform lists do not identify zones.

12.q: A dental nurse notices the image has overlapped premolar contacts but clearer molar contacts. Which interpretation is most accurate?
o: Horizontal angulation was slightly incorrect and centred away from premolar contacts
Exposure time was too short only in the premolar region
The patient moved only the premolars
12.w: Partial overlap in one region suggests beam alignment was slightly off-centre, missing some contact points while others remained open.

n.1: Exposure time affects the whole image, not one region selectively.
n.2: A reversed receptor would create a characteristic pattern across the image.
n.3: Movement does not isolate only premolar contacts in this way.
n.4: Processing faults affect image quality globally.

12.q: Which feature in the image most strongly indicates positioning error rather than angulation error?
o: The lower root tips extend beyond the image border
12.w: When anatomy is simply excluded from the receptor area, this most strongly indicates positioning error.

n.1: Unusually long teeth would suggest elongation.
n.2: Overlapped contacts suggest horizontal angulation error.
n.3: Blur indicates movement.
n.4: Crown density changes do not indicate positioning specifically.

12.q: A glass slab is not dried before cement mixing, and moisture remains on the surface. Why is this poor equipment preparation?
o: Extra moisture can alter the intended powder-liquid ratio and handling
It will improve the film thickness automatically
It makes the cement more radiopaque
It prevents the cement from adhering to the restoration
It guarantees a longer working time without affecting properties
12.w: Residual moisture can change the mix consistency and affect the setting characteristics of moisture-sensitive cements.

n.1: Film thickness is not predictably improved by contamination with water.
n.2: Radiopacity is not determined by surface moisture.
n.3: Adhesion effects are not the primary issue described here.
n.4: Although handling may change, the properties are not reliably preserved.

12.q: A patient presents with exposed root surfaces due to recession. What is the best action to reduce sensitivity?
12.w: Desensitising agents help block dentinal tubules and reduce sensitivity.

n.0: Enamel polishing does not address exposed roots.
n.2: Removing dentine worsens sensitivity.
n.3: Extraction is unnecessary for sensitivity alone.
n.4: Increased brushing can worsen recession.

12.q: During an oral examination, a structure is identified as forming the anterior roof of the mouth and consisting of bone. What is this structure?
12.w: The hard palate forms the anterior bony roof of the oral cavity.

n.0: The soft palate is posterior and not bony.
n.2: The uvula is a soft tissue extension of the soft palate.
n.3: The tongue is located on the floor of the mouth.
n.4: The floor of the mouth is inferior, not part of the roof.

12.q: Which sign most suggests trauma from over-instrumentation after treatment?
12.w: Soft tissue laceration suggests traumatic instrumentation.

n.1: Reduced plaque score is beneficial, not traumatic.
n.2: Taste does not indicate trauma.
n.3: Blood pressure is unrelated.
n.4: Occlusion is unrelated here.

12.q: A dental nurse incorrectly records a lower right canine as 43. What is the correct FDI number?
12.w: The lower right canine is correctly recorded as 43, so there is no error.

n.0: 33 refers to the lower left canine.
n.1: 13 refers to the upper right canine.
n.2: 23 refers to the upper left canine.
n.3: 44 refers to the lower right first premolar.

12.q: A nervous patient says they never understand dental advice because too much information is given at once. What is the best approach?
o: Give one clear message at a time
Provide all advice as one lecture
12.w: Breaking advice into clear manageable points improves understanding and recall.

n.1: Technical language may reduce understanding.
n.2: Too much information at once can overwhelm patients.
n.3: Speaking faster may reduce comprehension.
n.4: Questions help clarify understanding and should be encouraged.

12.q: Which statement best describes confidentiality in dental practice?
o: Patient information should be protected and shared only appropriately
It ends once treatment is complete
It is optional if the practice is busy
12.w: Confidentiality requires protecting personal information and limiting disclosure to appropriate circumstances.

n.0: Many forms of patient information are confidential, not only notes.
n.2: It applies to all patients.
n.3: Duties continue after treatment ends.
n.4: Workload does not remove confidentiality duties.

12.q: Why is suction particularly important during a surgical extraction?
12.w: Suction removes blood and fluids to maintain visibility for the operator.

n.1: Suction does not whiten teeth.
n.2: Pulp size is unaffected.
n.3: Sutures are not strengthened by suction.
n.4: Instrument sterilisation occurs separately.

12.q: Which practice most clearly breaks one-way workflow principles?
o: Returning dirty trays through clean side
12.w: Dirty items should not pass back through the clean side once segregation routes are established.

n.0: Moving dirty items to the sink is expected.
n.2: Drying cleaned items can be appropriate.
n.3: Labelling clean shelves supports organisation.
n.4: Date checking supports stock control.

12.q: What is the best sequence after trying in a denture for fit and appearance?
12.w: Any required changes should be clearly recorded for the next stage.

n.1: Further planning is needed before dismissal.
n.2: The denture should not be discarded.
n.3: Forceps are unrelated.
n.4: Plaster mixing is not the immediate clinical step.

12.q: Examine the radiograph. Which limitation is most associated with this radiographic type?
o: High level of image distortion and reduced detail compared to intraoral radiographs
Restricted view limited to posterior teeth only
Excessive radiation dose compared to all other techniques
12.w: Panoramic radiographs provide a broad overview but have lower resolution and increased distortion compared to intraoral radiographs.

n.0: Root apices are visible on panoramic radiographs, though with less detail.
n.2: Panoramic images include the full dentition, not just posterior teeth.
n.3: Bone levels can be assessed, though less precisely than with bitewings.
n.4: Panoramic radiographs do not necessarily have the highest radiation dose compared to all techniques.

12.q: Which arrangement best supports one-way decontamination workflow?
o: Dirty intake to clean storage sequence
12.w: A clear progression from dirty intake through processing to clean storage supports safe one-way flow.

n.0: Sink areas are unsuitable for sterile stock.
n.2: Mixed benches increase contamination risk.
n.3: Waste should be separated from clean items.
n.4: Crossing routes undermine segregation.

12.q: The image shows a cavitated lesion. Which term best describes this stage?
12.w: Cavitation indicates dentine involvement and irreversible damage.

n.0: Reversible lesions are non-cavitated.
n.1: Initial caries does not involve cavitation.
n.3: Arrested lesions are inactive.
n.4: This is not a healthy surface.

12.q: A patient says they brush immediately after frequent fizzy drinks because they want to protect their teeth. Which advice is most appropriate?
o: Delay brushing for a period after acidic drinks and rinse with water first
Brush harder immediately after each drink
Use mouthwash straight after the drink instead of brushing ever again
Skip all brushing on days acidic drinks are taken
Use a medium brush and scrub affected areas
12.w: Brushing immediately after acid exposure may increase wear; delaying and rinsing first is preferable.

n.1: Immediate vigorous brushing may increase erosive wear.
n.2: Mouthwash does not replace normal toothbrushing.
n.3: Regular brushing should continue with sensible timing.
n.4: Scrubbing after acid exposure is not recommended.

12.q: Which action best restores zone control after accidental mixing of clean and dirty trays?
12.w: The process should stop so trays can be separated and any compromised items assessed.

n.0: Continuing may spread contamination.
n.2: Visual judgement of cleanliness is unreliable.
n.3: Later relabelling does not control immediate risk.
n.4: Brief mixing can still compromise zones.

12.q: During CPR, the chest is not returning fully to its normal position between compressions. What is the error that should be corrected?
o: Leaning on the chest between compressions
12.w: Leaning prevents full chest recoil, reducing venous return and CPR effectiveness.

n.1: Frequent changes can be managed well and do not specifically cause poor recoil.
n.2: Early AED use is beneficial, not the issue described.
n.3: Oxygen timing does not explain lack of recoil.
n.4: Counting aloud may help coordination and is not the error shown.

12.q: A Class II restoration is being prepared and the dentist asks for the device that secures a matrix band around the tooth. Which instrument type is needed?
12.w: A matrix retainer holds and tightens a matrix band around the tooth during restoration placement.

n.1: An amalgam well is a container used to hold mixed amalgam.
n.2: A dappen dish holds small amounts of liquid or paste.
n.3: An excavator is used to remove soft carious dentine.
n.4: A shade guide is used for colour matching.

12.q: Which postoperative advice is most appropriate after extraction?
12.w: Avoiding rinsing initially helps protect the forming clot.

n.1: Smoking increases complication risk.
n.2: Suction from straws may disturb the clot.
n.3: Vigorous exercise may increase bleeding.
n.4: Touching the socket can disrupt healing.

12.q: From the image, which structure lies directly beneath enamel?
12.w: Dentine forms the bulk of the tooth and lies directly under enamel.

n.0: The pulp is deeper.
n.2: Cementum is on the root.
n.3: Gingiva is external soft tissue.
n.4: Bone surrounds the tooth, not beneath enamel.

12.q: A team member wears long artificial nails under gloves. Why is this poor PPE practice?
o: They increase glove damage risk and hinder effective hand hygiene
12.w: Artificial nails can puncture gloves and harbour microorganisms, compromising hand hygiene.

n.1: Grip is not the infection-control concern.
n.2: Apron fastening is unrelated.
n.3: Nails do not directly determine mask fit.
n.4: They do not sterilise anything.

12.q: What is the main risk of leaving waste bags in an evacuation route?
o: They may obstruct escape and create hazards
12.w: Waste must not block escape routes or create trip hazards.

n.0: Appearance is not the main safety concern.
n.2: Internet speed is unrelated.
n.3: They do not improve ventilation meaningfully.
n.4: Contracts are not the principal issue.

12.q: Which finding most strongly suggests poor denture retention?
12.w: Movement during function often indicates poor retention or stability.

n.1: A shiny surface does not indicate retention quality.
n.2: Pink acrylic colour is normal.
n.3: Clasps alone do not confirm poor retention.
n.4: Storage location is unrelated.

12.q: A patient becomes unresponsive in the waiting area, is not breathing normally, and no pulse is detected. What is the most appropriate immediate action?
o: Begin chest compressions and call for the AED
Place the patient in the recovery position
Give high-flow oxygen and observe for response
Check the pulse again for a full minute
Move the patient to the dental chair before acting
12.w: When a patient is unresponsive, not breathing normally and has no pulse, CPR should start immediately while another team member retrieves the AED.

n.1: Recovery position is only appropriate for a breathing unconscious patient.
n.2: Oxygen may be helpful later, but delaying compressions reduces survival chances.
n.3: Pulse checks should be brief; prolonged reassessment delays CPR.
n.4: Moving the patient first wastes critical time unless the environment is unsafe.

12.q: Which record is most useful when arranging licensed waste collection?
12.w: Waste transfer/consignment documentation supports compliant collection and traceability.

n.0: Tea rotas are unrelated.
n.2: Holiday calendars are unrelated.
n.3: Recall lists are unrelated.
n.4: Window cleaning logs are unrelated.

12.q: Which observation most strongly suggests gloves are the wrong size?
o: Frequent tearing when donned and restricted movement
12.w: Tearing on donning and poor dexterity commonly indicate incorrect sizing.

n.1: Warmth alone does not indicate size error.
n.2: Powder-free status does not indicate fit.
n.3: Colour is irrelevant.
n.4: Apron use does not indicate glove size.

12.q: Which behaviour most increases IRMER-related mistakes in practice?
o: Rushing and bypassing identification or positioning checks
12.w: Rushing often leads to wrong-patient, positioning or repeat-exposure errors.

n.0: Checklists help reduce mistakes.
n.2: Evaluation supports quality improvement.
n.3: Logs support compliance and maintenance.
n.4: Following rules reduces risk.

12.q: What is the best action if clean and dirty trays are accidentally swapped?
12.w: Workflow errors should be stopped immediately and items correctly re-segregated before continuing.

n.0: Brief mixing can still create contamination risk.
n.2: Assuming one tray is still clean may be unsafe.
n.3: Urgent labels do not resolve contamination concerns.
n.4: Handles are not the only possible contaminated surfaces.

12.q: Which aspect of interpretation is most affected by the fault seen on this panoramic radiograph?
o: Assessment of root outlines and surrounding bony detail
Counting the number of erupted teeth
Recognising the presence of the mandible
Identifying that the image is panoramic
Seeing that restorations may be present
12.w: Blur primarily reduces fine detail, making root morphology and surrounding bone assessment less reliable.

n.1: Tooth counting may still be possible despite reduced sharpness.
n.2: The mandible remains recognisable even with some blur.
n.3: The image type can still be identified despite movement.
n.4: Larger restorations may still be visible even when detail is reduced.

12.q: The lesion in the image appears cavitated. What does this indicate?
12.w: Cavitation indicates irreversible destruction of tooth structure.

n.0: Cavitation is beyond reversible stages.
n.1: Stains do not involve structural breakdown.
n.3: Fluoride uptake prevents caries.
n.4: Plaque alone does not indicate cavitation.

12.q: Which finding most strongly suggests improved adaptation to new dentures?
12.w: Increasing comfort commonly suggests improving adaptation.

n.1: More ulcers suggest problems.
n.2: Worsening clicking suggests instability.
n.3: Persistent speech problems need review.
n.4: Stopping wear suggests poor adaptation.

12.q: Why are jaw relation records taken during complete denture construction?
12.w: Jaw relation records help establish the correct occlusal relationship.

n.1: Pulp vitality is unrelated.
n.2: Implant torque is unrelated here.
n.3: Pocket depths are periodontal records.
n.4: This is unrelated to whitening.

12.q: Several mandibular periapicals in one session show the same long-root appearance as this image. What is the most likely cause?
o: The tubehead is repeatedly positioned with too shallow a vertical angle
12.w: Repeated elongation usually indicates the operator is consistently using insufficient vertical angulation.

n.1: Exhausted chemicals affect density and contrast, not image length.
n.2: Swallowing may create movement blur, not elongation.
n.3: Packet contamination does not create geometric distortion.
n.4: Timer faults alter exposure rather than tooth proportions.

12.q: Which feature in the image confirms that the lesion is active rather than arrested?
12.w: Active lesions are soft, discoloured, and often cavitated.

n.0: Hard surfaces suggest arrested lesions.
n.1: Smooth enamel is healthy.
n.3: Uniform colour indicates no lesion.
n.4: Plaque is typically present in active lesions.

12.q: Which feature in the image indicates chronic rather than acute infection?
12.w: A draining sinus suggests a chronic abscess.

n.0: Redness is seen in both acute and chronic cases.
n.1: Swelling can occur in both.
n.3: Sharp pain is more acute.
n.4: Temperature sensitivity relates to pulpitis.

12.q: A bur is found loose in a drawer. What is the best action?
o: Handle carefully and place it into an appropriate sharps container
Leave it for the next user
Wrap it in tissue and place in domestic waste
Put it in the sink tray
12.w: Loose contaminated burs should be handled safely and disposed of appropriately as sharps if single-use or unsuitable for reprocessing.

n.0: Unknown status items should not be returned to stock.
n.2: Leaving it creates risk.
